content.title: About
content.content: Graham crackers are dry baked biscuits made from whole‑wheat flour, sugar, honey and vegetable oil. They have a light sweet note, a crisp texture and are often used in desserts such as cheesecakes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Originally developed in the United States at the end of the 19th century as a healthier alternative to sweet cookies.
The name comes from the “Graham” brand, founded by Sylvester Graham, who promoted whole‑grain foods.
They are a key component of the classic American treat “s’mores” – layered with melted chocolate and toasted marshmallows.
Traditional recipes use whole‑wheat flour, retaining bran and germ.
Graham crackers can be found in both sweet and mildly salty versions, depending on the recipe.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Graham crackers supply iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many sweet cookies, they contain a modest amount of fat.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole grains deliver B1, B3 and folate, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: The whole‑grain base leads to a steadier rise in blood sugar than refined white bread.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with gluten intolerance or wheat allergy may experience reactions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some varieties contain added sugar, which may be a concern for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Savory versions can be relatively high in salt, which should be considered in hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Graham crackers can be enjoyed as a snack, used as a base for desserts (cheesecake, s’mores), crumbled into yogurt, mixed with dried fruit, or employed as a coating for frying.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage, refrigerate to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
